issues.issue: Citations are somewhat clustered — several sections (e.g., Traditional Pressed Hash, Dry-Sift) have no inline citations at all, leaving factual claims unsupported in those paragraphs
issues.fix: Add inline citations [[1]](#user-content-fn-1) or [[4]](#user-content-fn-4) to the Traditional Pressed Hash and Dry-Sift sections where THC ranges and terpene claims are made without citation

issues.issue: Leafly and Weedmaps are consumer-facing databases, not authoritative research sources — using them as citation anchors for potency data (40–65% THC) weakens scientific credibility
issues.fix: Supplement or replace citations [[1]](#user-content-fn-1) and [[2]](#user-content-fn-2) with peer-reviewed sources such as NCBI or a cannabis testing laboratory white paper for THC range claims

issues.issue: NORML is primarily a policy and advocacy organization — citing it for historical context is appropriate, but it is used in the consumer guidance section where a more neutral education source would be stronger
issues.fix: Reserve citation [[4]](#user-content-fn-4) for historical or policy claims only, and add a cannabis education or academic source for the dispensary-shopping guidance paragraph

issues.issue: The meta description is strong but runs approximately 158 characters — right at the upper boundary; some search engines may truncate it
issues.fix: Trim to 150 characters or fewer: 'From pressed kief to bubble hash and rosin, learn cannabis hash types, their THC levels, terpene profiles, and how to choose the right one.'

issues.issue: No FAQ section or FAQ schema markup is present — hash-related searches often trigger People Also Ask boxes that an FAQ section could capture
issues.fix: Add a short FAQ section (3–5 questions) covering common queries like 'What is the strongest type of hash?', 'Is bubble hash better than kief?', and 'Is hash stronger than weed?' using H3 headings for each question

issues.issue: The article states hash rosin tests at 65–80% THC, but premium live rosin products can occasionally exceed 80% — the ceiling may undersell top-tier commercial products
issues.fix: Adjust the rosin THC range to '65–85% THC' with a note that results vary significantly by source material quality and press conditions

issues.issue: The beginner recommendation points to 'traditional hash or lower-grade dry-sift' but does not address consumption method guidance — beginners may not know how to consume hash safely
issues.fix: Add one to two sentences in the beginner bullet point advising new consumers to start with a small amount, use a pipe or vaporizer rather than a joint mixed with hash, and wait to assess effects before consuming more

issues.issue: The terpene bullet list uses bold inline labels effectively, but the list itself has no introductory context connecting it explicitly to specific hash types — a reader skimming may miss which terpenes belong to which hash category
issues.fix: Add a brief parenthetical or sub-note after each terpene bullet indicating which hash type it is most commonly associated with, e.g., '— common in traditional Afghani pressed hash' already done for myrcene; replicate this pattern consistently for all four
